# Corpus Anatomy Atlas

> Open educational human anatomy atlas featuring 74 illustrated study chapters, 1,586 documented anatomical structures, 40 microscopic tissue lenses, a 206-bone skeletal inventory, and 312 muscles.

## Core Sections
- [Interactive Atlas Home](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/): Interactive body map, layered human anatomy showcase, and Corpus AI Assistant.
- [Anatomy Study Guides Hub](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/): Full index of 74 long-form anatomical & physiological study guides.
- [About & Editorial Policy](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/about.html): Educational scope, citation standards, and contact information.
- [Privacy Policy](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/privacy.html): Privacy and cookie disclosure.

## All 74 Anatomy Study Guides
- [Heart (Cor)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/heart/): A four-chambered muscular pump with four valves and its own electrical conduction system.
- [Lungs (Pulmones)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/lungs/): Two elastic, pleura-lined organs where air and blood come within 0.5 µm of each other.
- [Brain (Encephalon)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/brain/): Midsagittal section: cerebrum, diencephalon, brainstem and cerebellum around the ventricular system.
- [Kidney (Ren)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/kidney/): Coronal section plus a nephron: filtration, reabsorption, secretion and urine concentration.
- [Liver (Hepar)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/liver/): The body's chemical plant: metabolism, bile, clotting factors, detoxification and storage.
- [Stomach & intestines (Gaster et intestina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/gut/): The gastrointestinal tract from oesophagus to rectum, with the villus that does the absorbing.
- [Eye (Oculus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/eye/): Sagittal section: an optical instrument that focuses light onto a neural film.
- [Ear (Auris)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/ear/): A pressure-wave collector that turns vibration into nerve impulses and doubles as a gyroscope.
- [Pancreas (Pancreas)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/pancreas/): A dual gland: digestive enzymes from acini, hormones from the islets of Langerhans.
- [Spleen (Lien (splen))](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/spleen/): The largest lymphoid organ: a blood filter, immune sentinel and red-cell graveyard.
- [Thyroid gland (Glandula thyroidea)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/thyroid/): A butterfly gland of follicles that sets the body's metabolic rate.
- [Urinary bladder (Vesica urinaria)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/bladder/): A detrusor-muscle reservoir with a smooth trigone and a two-stage sphincter.
- [Skin (Cutis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/skin/): A layered barrier with hair, glands, receptors and its own immune system.
- [Spinal cord (Medulla spinalis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/spinalcord/): Cross-section: a grey butterfly inside white tracts, wrapped in three meninges.
- [Male reproductive system (Organa genitalia masculina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/male/): Sperm production in the scrotum, maturation in the epididymis, and a shared exit with urine.
- [Female reproductive system (Organa genitalia feminina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/female/): A cyclic system: ovulation, fertilisation in the tube, implantation in the endometrium.
- [Male body — anterior (Corpus masculinum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/malebody/): A glass-body view of the male: every major organ in place, from brain to testes, with the reproductive tract in the pelvis.
- [Female body — anterior (Corpus femininum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/femalebody/): A glass-body view of the female: major organs in place, with breasts, uterus and ovaries completing the picture.
- [Nervous system — overview (Systema nervosum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/nervous/): One continuous network: the brain and spinal cord compute, and 43 pairs of peripheral nerves carry orders out and reports back.
- [Nervous system — male (Systema nervosum (vir))](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/nervousmale/): The male figure with every nerve pathway highlighted — same wiring as the female page, shown on male proportions for side-by-side study.
- [Nervous system — female (Systema nervosum (femina))](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/nervousfemale/): The female figure with every nerve pathway highlighted — study pelvic plexus branching on female proportions.
- [Cranial nerves (Nervi craniales I–XII)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/cranialnerves/): Twelve pairs leave the brain directly — smell to tongue movement — and they are examined in strict order in every neurological exam.
- [Autonomic nervous system (Systema nervosum autonomicum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/autonomic/): The unconscious half of the nervous system: sympathetic accelerator, parasympathetic brake, and the gut's own enteric brain.
- [Breast (Mamma / Glandula mammaria)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/breast/): A modified sweat gland: glandular lobules make milk, ducts carry it, fat gives shape, and lymph drains mostly to the axilla — which is why breast cancer staging checks axillary nodes.
- [Skeleton (Systema skeletale)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/skeleton/): The frame: leverage for muscle, armour for viscera, a calcium bank, and the marrow factory that makes every blood cell.
- [Muscular system (Systema musculare)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/muscle/): Every movement, every breath, every heartbeat's preload begins as muscle fibres sliding — here the skeletal set in écorché.
- [Lymphatic system (Systema lymphoideum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/lymph/): The body's drainage and defence network: interstitial fluid returns as lymph, filtered node by node, while immune cells patrol.
- [Vascular system (Systema cardiovasculare)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/vascular/): Two trees from one pump: arteries deliver under pressure, veins return against gravity — with valves, shunts and plexuses throughout.
- [Endocrine system (Systema endocrinum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/endocrine/): The body's slow wiring: hormones released straight into blood to tune metabolism, growth, stress, salt, sugar and reproduction.
- [Joints & ligaments (Articulationes et ligamenta)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/joints/): Where bones meet: cartilage cushions, capsules contain, ligaments guide — the knee is the classic teaching joint because every principle is visible in it.
- [Shoulder joint (Articulatio humeri)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/shoulder/): Mobility bought at the price of stability: a shallow glenoid, a loose capsule, and four rotator-cuff tendons doing the holding.
- [Upper airway (Via aerea superior)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/larynx/): The conducting corridor: nose conditions the air, pharynx crosses food and air, larynx turns air into voice and guards the lungs, trachea delivers.
- [Bone marrow & blood (Medulla ossium)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/marrow/): The hidden factory: red marrow makes two million blood cells per second; yellow marrow stores energy; both sit behind bone you see every day.
- [Male pelvis & perineum (Pelvis masculina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/malepelvis/): The male pelvic floor in sagittal section: bladder, prostate and urethra in front, rectum and anal canal behind, and the muscular sheet that holds them up.
- [Female pelvis & perineum (Pelvis femina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/femalepelvis/): The female pelvic floor in sagittal section: bladder and urethra, vagina and anteverted uterus, rectum behind — plus the ligaments and pouches that position them.
- [Uterus — layers & cavity (Uterus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/gynuterus/): The womb in cross-section: endometrium, junctional zone, myometrium, cavity, isthmus and the key clinical boundaries.
- [Cervix — transformation zone (Cervix uteri)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/gyncervix/): The gynecology examination landmark: external os, canal, squamocolumnar junction and transformation zone in one close-up.
- [Ovary & uterine tube (Ovarium et tuba uterina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/gynadnexa/): From follicular cortex to ampulla: the ovary, fimbriae, tubal mucosal folds and the hidden routes of fertilization.
- [Vagina — walls & fornices (Vagina)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/gynvagina/): A layered fibromuscular canal: rugae, muscularis, fornices, vestibular opening, adjacent urethra and rectum.
- [Vulva — external genital anatomy (Vulva)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/gynvulva/): The external genitalia, carefully distinguished from the vagina: labia, clitoral complex, vestibule, openings, glands and perineum.
- [Pelvic support & surgical planes (Fascia et ligamenta pelvis feminae)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/gynsupport/): The surgical map: ureter under uterine artery, uterosacral and cardinal supports, broad ligament folds, ovarian pedicle and pelvic floor.
- [Testis & epididymis — microanatomy (Testis et epididymis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/maletestis/): The sperm-production organ from tunica through seminiferous tubule to rete, efferent ducts and epididymal tail.
- [Prostate, ducts & penis (Prostata et penis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/maleprostate/): Prostatic zones and the urinary–ejaculatory crossing: urethra, verumontanum, ducts, seminal vesicles and erectile bodies.
- [Clitoral erectile complex (Clitoris · corpora cavernosa et bulbi vestibuli)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/clitoralcomplex/): A three-dimensional neurovascular and erectile complex: paired crura, body, glans and closely related vestibular bulbs.
- [Penile erectile tissue (Corpora cavernosa · corpus spongiosum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/penileerectile/): Two dorsal cavernous bodies and one ventral spongiosum carry arterial, neural and urethral pathways through the penis.
- [Skin layers & appendages (Epidermis · dermis · tela subcutanea)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/skinlayers/): The five thick-skin epidermal strata, two dermal zones, hypodermis, receptors and follicle–gland units.
- [Facial nerve · CN VII (Nervus facialis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/facialnerve/): Track facial motor branches, taste, lacrimation and salivation through the temporal bone and parotid gland.
- [Trigeminal nerve · CN V (Nervus trigeminus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/trigeminalnerve/): Map facial sensation and masticatory motor fibers without confusing trigeminal CN V with facial CN VII.
- [Eye · microscopic layers (Bulbus oculi · tunicae oculi)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/eyeanatomy/): Three ocular coats, five classical corneal layers, aqueous route, lens suspension, macula and optic disc.
- [Retina · neural microanatomy (Retina neurosensorialis · epithelium pigmentosum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/retina/): Rods, cones, bipolar and ganglion circuits; fovea, optic disc, pigment epithelium and dual blood supply.
- [Nephron · kidney microanatomy (Nephron · corpusculum renale)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/nephron/): Follow filtration through glomerular barrier, segmented tubules, medullary loop and collecting ducts.
- [Brachial plexus · arm nerves (Plexus brachialis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/brachialplexus/): Trace the arm nerve network from spinal roots through trunks, divisions and cords to five terminal nerves.
- [Cerebrum · cortex & deep pathways (Cortex cerebri · substantia alba · nuclei basales)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/cerebraldeep/): Trace cortex, white matter, corpus callosum, basal nuclei and thalamus on a realistic coronal section.
- [Meninges, CSF & venous sinuses (Meninges · liquor cerebrospinalis · sinus durae matris)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/meningescsf/): Follow dura, arachnoid and pia; then CSF from choroid plexus to subarachnoid drainage.
- [Brainstem & cerebellar circuitry (Truncus encephali · cerebellum)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/brainstemdeep/): Locate brainstem levels, cranial-nerve nuclei, pyramids and cerebellar peduncles, cortex and nuclei.
- [Pulmonary acinus · gas-exchange barrier (Acinus pulmonis · alveoli)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/pulmonaryacinus/): From terminal bronchiole to alveolar sac, type I/II pneumocytes, macrophages and the air–blood barrier.
- [Hepatic lobule · liver microanatomy (Lobulus hepatis · acinus hepatis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/hepaticlobule/): See portal triad, central vein, sinusoidal cells and the opposite directions of blood and bile.
- [Small intestine · wall & enteric plexuses (Tunicae intestini tenuis · plexus enterici)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/intestinalwall/): Map villus–crypt renewal, epithelial cell types, capillaries and lacteals, plus two enteric nerve plexuses.
- [Skull & facial bones (Ossa cranii et faciei)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/skullface/): Name every one of the 14 facial and 8 cranial bones, with accurate visible labels and deeper views for hidden structures.
- [Teeth · dental anatomy (Dentes permanentes et decidui)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/dentition/): Follow crown-to-root layers, 32 permanent and 20 primary tooth positions, class shapes, FDI/Universal numbers and dental sensory nerves.
- [Anatomical language · planes & movement (Terminologia anatomica)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/anatomicallanguage/): Learn patient right and left, body planes, directional terms and movements; the colored reference planes are labelled only where visibly shown.
- [Body cavities · regions & quadrants (Cavitates et regiones corporis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/bodyregions/): Trace dorsal and ventral cavities, serous spaces and patient-oriented abdominal quadrants and regions.
- [Cells & four basic tissues (Cellulae et textus fundamentales)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/tissuefoundations/): Explore cell structure and the four tissue families with dedicated microscopic-scale teaching illustrations.
- [Sperm cell · anatomy & production (Spermatozoon et spermatogenesis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/spermanatomy/): A separate sperm chapter: head, midpiece, flagellum, meiosis, Sertoli support and epididymal maturation.
- [Egg cell · oocyte & ovulation (Oocytus secundarius et ovulatio)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/oocyteanatomy/): A separate egg chapter: primary versus secondary oocyte, meiosis, zona pellucida, corona radiata and ovulation.
- [Fertilization · sperm meets oocyte (Fecundatio)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/fertilization/): Follow sperm transit, capacitation, zona interaction, membrane fusion and formation of the diploid zygote.
- [Zygote to blastocyst · early divisions (Segmentatio et blastocystis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/cleavageblastocyst/): Trace the separate preimplantation chapter: zygote, cleavage, morula, blastocoel and hatching.
- [Implantation · blastocyst in endometrium (Implantatio blastocystis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/implantation/): Separate implantation stage: endometrial receptivity, hatching, trophoblast invasion and early hCG.
- [Placenta · maternal–fetal exchange (Placenta et membranae fetales)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/placentaanatomy/): Separate placenta chapter: chorionic villi, decidua, separated circulations, cord and membranes.
- [Embryo · early organ formation (Embryogenesis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/embryodevelopment/): Separate embryonic chapter: germ layers, neurulation, folding, early heart and limb buds before fetal growth.
- [Fetus · growth & pregnancy trimesters (Periodus fetalis)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/fetaldevelopment/): Follow fetal growth, placenta, organs and first, second and third trimester landmarks without confusing pregnancy weeks and conception age.
- [Labor stage 1 · cervix dilates (Partus prima periodus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/laborfirststage/): Separate first-stage birth chapter: uterine contractions, cervical effacement and dilation to complete opening.
- [Labor stage 2 · birth of baby (Partus secunda periodus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/laborsecondstage/): Separate second-stage birth chapter: full dilation, fetal descent, rotation and delivery of the baby.
- [Labor stage 3 · delivery of placenta (Partus tertia periodus)](https://corpus-anatomy-atlas.netlify.app/learn/laborthirdstage/): Separate third-stage birth chapter: placental separation, uterine contraction, membranes and postpartum bleeding awareness.
